nodes.name: Journal Entry - Tuesday, March 31, 2026
nodes.filePreview:
The same themes kept surfacing: work stress, sleep, running, budgeting, and trying to live with intention.
I sketched a StoryGraph approach that gives equal weight to small habits and major moments.
I left feeling like Riverwalk this weekend could be the right start to April.

nodes.name: Journal Entry - Friday, April 3, 2026
nodes.filePreview:
We talked about financial anxiety and why budgeting helps me feel less out of control.
Maya reviewed my StoryGraph draft and told me not to sanitize the ordinary parts of life.
Sleep has been inconsistent this week, and it shows up in my patience more than anything else.

nodes.name: Journal Entry - Monday, April 6, 2026
nodes.filePreview:
Jordan suggested protecting mornings for deep work, and I think he is right.
I used that idea to restructure my StoryGraph work blocks and got more done than expected.
Grabbed coffee at Maple Street Cafe and wrote about work stress triggers before they blurred together.

nodes.name: Journal Entry - Thursday, April 9, 2026
nodes.filePreview:
When sleep falls apart, everything else follows: work stress spikes, running drops, and budgeting gets sloppy.
I tracked spending tonight and saw the same leaks again, especially convenience spending on rushed days.
A short walk near Riverwalk helped me reset enough to close the day without doom-scrolling.

nodes.name: Journal Entry - Sunday, April 12, 2026
nodes.filePreview:
The sleep-work stress connection keeps repeating: bad sleep makes normal feedback feel like criticism.
I organized StoryGraph notes in the afternoon and tagged the same themes that keep reappearing.
Ended the day at Maple Street Cafe with Lena talking about burnout and how to build kinder routines.

nodes.name: Journal Entry - Wednesday, April 15, 2026
nodes.filePreview:
I skipped late-night coding and chose sleep, even though part of me felt guilty about StoryGraph momentum.
Met Maya at Maple Street Cafe and we compared monthly budgeting habits and what actually sticks.
Work stress is still loud, but I noticed I am less reactive when I stop pretending I can outrun fatigue.

nodes.name: Journal Entry - Saturday, April 18, 2026
nodes.filePreview:
Coffee at Maple Street Cafe after the run turned into a long talk about boundaries, sleep, and work stress.
I drafted StoryGraph ideas around recurring people and recurring places, not just big events.
Budgeting check-in tonight looked decent except for delivery spending after late meetings.

nodes.name: Sometimes i wish I was a cat
nodes.filePreview:
Jordan called during lunch, and we admitted both of us are overbooked and pretending we are fine.
I spent an hour connecting nodes in StoryGraph and felt weirdly hopeful seeing names and patterns recur.
Ran into Lena at Maple Street Cafe and we set a soft plan for Riverwalk this weekend.

nodes.name: I cant wait for this weekend
nodes.filePreview: Lena met me at Riverwalk after a hard afternoons, and by the end I could breathe again. Work stress was high, but movement made it feel less personal and less permanent. Maya sent me comments on the StoryGraph journal map and said the repeated themes are finally visible. I stopped at Maple Street Cafe and reworked budgeting categories so groceries and takeout stop blurring together.

nodes.name: Mondays are for the birds
nodes.filePreview: I started the morning with my bestie Maya at Maple Street Cafe and felt less scattered before work even began. The day still had sharp edges, but work stress felt manageable because I actually slept last night. Jordan wants to do Riverwalk on Wednesday, and I said yes because running has been the one thing that steadies my head. I reviewed my budgeting sheet tonight and noticed I spend the most when I skip planning and eat reactively. I wrote a few StoryGraph notes about how tiny routines seem to predict the kind of day I get. awdawdawdaw
